newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-VICENZA DRAW RESTORES LEAD OVER INTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VICENZA DRAW RESTORES LEAD OVER INTER.

text.p: Alessandro Iannuzzi's first-half goal was enough to earn Vicenza a 1-1 draw at Perugia on Sunday and restore his side's historic one-point lead over Internazionale at the top of the Italian first division.

Vicenza, setting the pace in serie A for the first time in their 94-year existence, took the lead through Iannuzzi's 20-metre shot in the 10th minute before Carmine Gautieri levelled the scores for Perugia in the 33rd.
The vital away point leaves Vicenza with 21 points from 11 matches, one more than Inter who had briefly drawn level on Saturday after themselves drawing 2-2 at home to Cagliari.
But Intercontinental Cup winners Juventus moved ominously into third place after defeating Bologna, courtesy of Zinedine Zidane's superbly struck 50th minute freekick.
The Turin side are level on 19 points with Bologna, two behind Vicenza -- but have played a game less.

Pasquale Luiso's 71st minute goal -- his eighth of the season -- condemned Milan to a 3-2 defeat at lowly Piacenza after Frenchman Cristophe Dugarry's double strike had pulled the champions back from a 2-0 half-time deficit.
It was Milan's fourth defeat of the season and leaves them languishing in ninth place in the table, six points behind Vicenza.
